elements.element: If automatic renewal is not used, renewal occurs only by mutual written agreement.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent because § 8.2 uses automatic renewal; therefore, this alternative-route requirement is not operative.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, each automatic renewal term is twelve months.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 states that each Order Form renews for twelve months.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 requires sixty days' advance written notice, including from Customer, rather than no more than 30 days.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Vendor must provide a reminder 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no Vendor renewal-reminder obligation.

elements.element: Renewal price increases are capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 caps recurring Fee increases at the lesser of the preceding twelve-month CPI increase and 3%.
Section 8.2 provides that each Order Form renews unless a Party gives timely notice.

elements.element: The non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 requires exactly sixty days' advance written notice.

elements.element: Renewal price increases are capped at 5% or less.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 caps increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, which is no more than 5%.

result.reason: The redline minimally reduces the non-renewal window from 180 days to the fallback maximum of 60 days while retaining the compliant CPI/3% price cap. It therefore fully satisfies fallback. Preferred is not satisfied because Customer does not have a 30-day opt-out right and Vendor has no 60-day renewal-reminder duty. While the change is substantively effective, the markup appears to use an overlay/whiteout-style rendering rather than a clean native-text revision, which materially reduces drafting quality and creates avoidable execution and document-integrity risk.
